item.title: MW4 DMZ Player Count: How Many Players Per Match & Can You Play Solo?
item.description:
Modern Warfare 4 's DMZ mode can be ruthless, with challenging AI-controlled hostiles and aggressive player-controlled Operators hunting you down as you dare to complete ops and gather loot to exfil with. So you know what you're getting yourself into, we'll explain squad sizes, total player counts for the DMZ map, and how the solo queue works .

Modern Warfare 4: What Happens If You Die in DMZ?

DMZ is extremely challenging with its blend of PvPvE combat. Here's what you need to know about dying and getting your gear back.

By Jake Fillery

How Many Players Are There in MW4 DMZ?

There can be up to 20 squads and 60 players active on the DMZ map . This isn't Warzone, so don't expect to encounter enemy teams at every turn. At DMZ Player Level 20, you will encounter more hostile teams ; that's when the training wheels come off.

While you can queue as a solo player, you may still encounter teams of trios . While DMZ will try to prioritize other solo players, you might not always get lucky, and the lobby you enter may have teams ready to hunt you down and steal your loot.

Can You Play Solo in MW4 DMZ?

Yes, you can play DMZ as a solo player simply by hitting Deploy and hitting the opt-out button for Squad Fill . This ensures you will queue for a game without joining random players to make a trio, which in turn prioritizes you as a solo player in Hajin, so (hopefully) you experience other solo players .

How to Survive Solo in MW4 DMZ

Other Operators are extremely hostile and won't hesitate to shoot you first, and the AI-controlled enemies are no joke. Whether you're in a team or a solo player, some factors might help you to survive Hajin and exfil with your loot:

  • Tourniquet - This item can be used twice per match and sacrifices health to allow you to revive yourself.
    • You can acquire the lost health with a First Aid Kit.
    • AI-controlled enemies will ignore you when downed, but real players will execute you.

  • Trait Points can be used to gain advantages, like the Possum Trait to revive yourself when killed.
  • Stealth is key to surviving and avoiding hostile attention, so watch the stealth meter and avoid direct confrontations.

MW4 DMZ's Squad Sizes & Assimilation, Explained

You can have a total of 3 players in a squad starting from your FOB when you are in a Party or elect to opt in to Squad Fill. However, you can technically increase this party size to 4 if you assimilate with another squad you meet in Hajin.

Assimilating requires you to communicate with each other, and it's likely that any squad you run into is going to shoot first and ask questions later.

item.title: Pokemon's Mega Evolution Revival Makes Its Other Battle Gimmicks Feel Disposable
item.description:
Mega Evolution has always been one of my favorite battle mechanics in the Pokemon franchise, and its return in Pokemon Legends: Z-A is a reminder of why it stands out. Seeing a familiar Pokemon transform into a new form is exciting, particularly when it gives an underappreciated creature a chance to shine. With Pokemon GO continuing to develop Mega Evolution, the mechanic feels more relevant than ever, raising questions about how the franchise approaches its battle systems.

I understand why Game Freak introduces new gimmicks with each generation. They keep battles fresh, offer new strategic possibilities, and help distinguish each game's experience. However, I wonder whether Pokemon would benefit from developing Mega Evolution more consistently instead of introducing mechanics that largely disappear after one generation. I primarily experience the franchise through its video games rather than the Pokemon Trading Card Game, so my perspective has its limits. Still, Mega Evolution makes a compelling case for building on an established mechanic rather than continually replacing it.

All Pokemon Games With Mega Evolution

If you enjoy Mega Evolution in Pokemon, these games all let you utilize the powerful mechanic.

By Julián Jorge Fernández Loyarte

Mega Evolution Makes Familiar Pokemon Feel New

Introduced in Pokemon X and Pokemon Y , Mega Evolution allows certain Pokemon to transform temporarily during battle, gaining new appearances, increased stats, and sometimes different types or abilities. Mega Charizard X's black-and-blue design and Dragon typing gave Charizard a fresh take, while Mega Mawile made an already distinctive Pokemon even more memorable. These transformations offered more than a temporary power boost, encouraging players to reconsider creatures they might otherwise overlook.

My favorite new Mega Evolutions include Dragalge, Drampa, and Glimmora, three of my favorite Pokemon. Seeing them receive this attention makes the mechanic particularly exciting because it gives creatures I already care about another opportunity to stand out. Their appeal goes beyond becoming stronger; their new forms offer another reason to appreciate their designs and consider their battle potential. With such a large roster, Mega Evolution provides a way to revisit existing Pokemon without relying entirely on introducing new ones.

Pokemon Legends: Z-A Shows Mega Evolution's Potential

Pokemon Legends: Z-A puts Mega Evolution at the center of its experience, incorporating it into the story and battles through features such as Rogue Mega Evolutions. This makes the mechanic more than a nostalgic callback. It helps shape the adventure in Lumiose City and gives players a reason to engage with Mega Evolution beyond simply increasing their Pokemon's power.

The game's real-time combat also demonstrates how an established mechanic can evolve in a new context. Movement, timing, and positioning add fresh considerations without stripping away what makes Mega Evolution appealing. I would like to see more of this approach across the franchise. New games can introduce different settings and battle systems while still developing mechanics that players already enjoy. This system, along with Rogue Mega Evolutions, prove that revisiting a successful idea does not have to mean repeating it.

Pokemon GO Gives Mega Evolution Staying Power

Pokemon GO offers another example of how Mega Evolution can remain relevant beyond its original generation. Since introducing the mechanic in 2020, the mobile game has expanded it with features such as Mega Levels, rewarding players for repeatedly using and developing their Pokemon. This creates progression beyond individual battles and gives players reasons to invest in the mechanic over time.

Mega Evolution serves different purposes across the two games. In the main series, it can influence battle strategy and create dramatic encounters; in Pokemon GO (especially with the new Super Mega Raid system), it supports collection goals, raid participation, and progression. ​ ​ This flexibility suggests that Mega Evolution can work across different experiences without needing to function identically in each one. Rather than reserving it for occasional returns, the franchise could keep finding new ways to make it relevant.

Other Pokemon Battle Gimmicks Have Their Own Strengths

Dynamax and Gigantamax arrived in Pokemon Sword and Pokemon Shield , bringing spectacle through enormous Pokemon and powerful Max Moves. Gigantamax forms also offered unique designs for certain species. Z-Moves, introduced in Pokemon Sun and Pokemon Moon , delivered dramatic finishing attacks, while Terastallization in Pokemon Scarlet and Pokemon Violet added strategic depth by changing Pokemon's defensive typing and strengthening certain attacks.

These mechanics each have merits. Terastallization can dramatically change competitive matchups, while Dynamax and Z-Moves create memorable battle moments. Pokemon GO has also introduced Dynamax and Gigantamax, showing that mechanics can return outside the mainline games, and Terastallization could potentially follow in the future. The problem is not that these ideas lack value, but that their presence across the franchise can feel inconsistent. Giving more of these mechanics opportunities to return could help them feel like lasting parts of Pokemon rather than features tied to a single generation.

What To Read Next
New Pokemon Release Brings Back Shadow Pokemon and Mega Evolutions
Pokemon Legends: Z-A's Mega Heatran Officially Coming Back in December 2026
Pokemon GO Is Making Big Changes to Mega Evolution Charged Attacks

There is a good reason for Pokemon to keep experimenting. New mechanics encourage players to rethink familiar strategies, and each generation needs opportunities to offer something different. With Pokemon Winds and Waves on the horizon, the franchise does not need to stop introducing new gimmicks, but giving established mechanics a longer life could make its evolution feel more connected. Mega Evolution's revival shows that moving forward does not always require leaving a good idea behind.

Pokemon Legends: Z-A

item.title: Modern Warfare 4: What Happens If You Die in DMZ?
item.description:
Modern Warfare 4 | DMZ is here, and with it comes the consequence of death. Each time you drop into Hajin and die, you will be forced back to the FOB with your active Operator now classed as "Missing in Action". If you want to avoid losing your progress (and loot), then you need to know what comes next when you die in DMZ .

Modern Warfare 4: How to Get DMZ XP & All Level Unlocks

Your DMZ Level is separate to your Modern Warfare 4 rank. Here's the level cap, how to get DMZ XP, and what you'll earn for each level up.

By Jake Fillery

What Happens If You Die in DMZ (& Can You Get Your Stuff Back)?

If you are killed in DMZ, either by another Operator or an AI-controlled hostile, then you will be sent back to the Field Operations Base. Here, you will be given an option to rescue the Operator you died as. Choosing to rescue an Operator costs DMZ Cash, and the cost increases with each Trait you obtain from leveling the Dog Tags .

When you rescue a Missing in Action Operator, you will restore their Traits, Trait Points, and their Dog Tags . This means you won't lose progress toward Prestige. However, you will lose everything that was in your Loadout and your Pack, unless you had a Reserve Slot to keep one item safe upon death.

The more Trait Points you obtain, the more pricey it will be to rescue your Operators, so make sure you have plenty of DMZ Cash ready, as you never know who you might encounter in Hajin next.

If you decide not to rescue your Operator, then you can click Manage and dismiss them. This will allow you to select a new Operator, including different skins, but this will reset your Dog Tag progress to Steel I. However, choosing a different Operator will not reset your Stash or your DMZ Player Level.

item.title: Clash Royale: Best Power Surge Global Tournament Decks
item.description:
Clash Royale's new Power Surge Global Tournament is here. It runs from October 20 to 25 , and its Lightning mechanic can make things tricky if you don't plan your pushes well. You only get five losses before you are out, so choosing the right deck matters. There are also plenty of rewards that you can earn by winning matches. Here's how the Power Surge tournament works in Clash Royale , along with the best decks to use and some tips to help you get more wins.

Clash Royale: How to Get the Free Hero Electro Wizard Emote

Clash Royale players can claim a Hero Electro Wizard emote for free right now. Here's what you need to do.

By Umama Ali

​

Best Power Surge Decks in Clash Royale

Here are the most broken Power Surge decks right now:

Tesla X-Bow Siege

When I first tried the Power Surge tournament, I thought Siege decks would struggle because of all the Lightning strikes. But since buildings are immune to Lightning in this mode, I can see X-Bow being a strong pick.

​

The idea is simple: place your X-Bow and protect it. If you have enough elixir, you should put a Tesla next to it to help deal with enemy troops. Otherwise, Skeletons and Bats can help keep your X-Bow alive without spending too much Elixir. Earthquake is also handy for dealing with enemy buildings.

Dark Prince is another good fit in this Power Surge deck, thanks to its shield. Bats give you cheap air defense. I was tempted to use Archers for that classic X-Bow combo, but Bats are cheaper, and swarm cards are just better in this event. You also have the Log and Barbarian Barrel to deal with the swarms. Even after the X-Bow Tesla duo, this deck only costs 3.0 elixir.

I'm not really a Goblin Drill player, but I've managed to win quite a few matches with this deck. It's a good fit for Power Surge because some of its main cards can deal with the Lightning mechanic. The Goblin Drill doesn't get targeted by Lightning. Similarly, the Dark Prince's shield can absorb a strike without costing him any HP.

Your main plan is to keep putting pressure on your opponent with Goblin Drill and Dark Prince . Poison and Giant Snowball work well with the Gob Drill. Keep deploying the drill and use your spells when your opponent tries to stop it.

For your Evo and Hero slots, I'd go with Hero Dark Prince, Evo Tesla, and Evo Giant Snowball. Hero Dark Prince's ability can catch opponents off guard, while Evo Tesla gives you strong defense. The Evo Giant Snowball is also a good fit here because it can help your Goblin Drill get more damage.

Log Bait is not quite popular in the regular meta right now, but this deck can do well in Power Surge. Most of the cards are cheap, so you can keep the pressure on your opponent without spending too much elixir. Your main goal is to keep sending out Wall Breakers and Goblin Barrel to chip away at their tower. If your opponent uses a spell to counter them, Dart Goblin or Bats will be hard to stop.

I have made a few changes to the usual Log Bait deck to make this deck work better in Power Surge. The Princess and Evo Skeleton Army are out, replaced by Earthquake and Bats. I have also replaced the Hero Valkyrie with the Hero Knight to lower the deck's cost. And the Evo Tesla takes the place of the Cannon for stronger defense.

For your Evo and Hero slots, I'd go with Hero Knight, Evo Tesla, and Evo Goblin Barrel. Hero Knight is a great pick in pretty much any meta, and the Evo Tesla can handle a range of enemy pushes. Evo Goblin Barrel is also useful for sneaking in some damage if your opponent fails to spot the real barrel.

How Does Clash Royale’s Power Surge Global Tournament Work?

In the Power Surge tournament, Lightning strikes the arena every so often. It seems to happen roughly every 20 to 30 seconds , though I haven't timed it exactly. The good thing is that Lightning doesn't affect buildings in this mode, so your buildings and towers are safe from it.

You can earn different rewards by winning matches, including chests and Wild Cards. If you want to check your standing, you can tap the 'Wins' section in the middle of the screen to see the Hall of Fame and your tournament ranking.

You can only lose four matches before your tournament run ends, so make sure you choose a deck you can play comfortably.

​

Tips for Clash Royale’s Power Surge Global Tournament

Prefer Cheap Decks

Cheap decks can work really well in Power Surge, so consider swapping expensive cards for cheaper alternatives. For example, Archers cost less than Musketeer or Flying Machine, and all three can die to Lightning. You can cycle back to Archers faster without spending as much elixir. I'd avoid heavy tanks like Giant Skeleton since they will keep getting hit by Lightning and take a lot of damage.

Take Advantage of Buildings

Buildings are immune to Lightning in this mode, so don't be afraid to include them in your deck. I'd even consider running two buildings as they will give you more options on both offense and defense. Siege decks can also take advantage of this, but you will still need to protect your X-Bow or Mortar from enemy troops. The Earthquake is a useful spell to have if your opponent is doing the same thing.

Choose Cards That Can Handle Lightning

Keep Lightning in mind when choosing your cards. The Dark Prince is a good choice because its shield can take a Lightning strike without losing HP. Cheap cards like Bats and Skeletons are also useful since they don't cost much elixir. Even if Lightning takes them out, you won't lose much.

The idea is simple: place your X-Bow and protect it. If you have enough elixir, you should put a Tesla next to it to help deal with enemy troops. Otherwise, Skeletons and Bats can help keep your X-Bow alive without spending too much Elixir. Earthquake is also handy for dealing with enemy buildings.

Dark Prince is another good fit in this Power Surge deck, thanks to its shield. Bats give you cheap air defense. I was tempted to use Archers for that classic X-Bow combo, but Bats are cheaper, and swarm cards are just better in this event. You also have the Log and Barbarian Barrel to deal with the swarms. Even after the X-Bow Tesla duo, this deck only costs 3.0 elixir.

I'm not really a Goblin Drill player, but I've managed to win quite a few matches with this deck. It's a good fit for Power Surge because some of its main cards can deal with the Lightning mechanic. The Goblin Drill doesn't get targeted by Lightning. Similarly, the Dark Prince's shield can absorb a strike without costing him any HP.

Your main plan is to keep putting pressure on your opponent with Goblin Drill and Dark Prince . Poison and Giant Snowball work well with the Gob Drill. Keep deploying the drill and use your spells when your opponent tries to stop it.

For your Evo and Hero slots, I'd go with Hero Dark Prince, Evo Tesla, and Evo Giant Snowball. Hero Dark Prince's ability can catch opponents off guard, while Evo Tesla gives you strong defense. The Evo Giant Snowball is also a good fit here because it can help your Goblin Drill get more damage.

Log Bait is not quite popular in the regular meta right now, but this deck can do well in Power Surge. Most of the cards are cheap, so you can keep the pressure on your opponent without spending too much elixir. Your main goal is to keep sending out Wall Breakers and Goblin Barrel to chip away at their tower. If your opponent uses a spell to counter them, Dart Goblin or Bats will be hard to stop.

I have made a few changes to the usual Log Bait deck to make this deck work better in Power Surge. The Princess and Evo Skeleton Army are out, replaced by Earthquake and Bats. I have also replaced the Hero Valkyrie with the Hero Knight to lower the deck's cost. And the Evo Tesla takes the place of the Cannon for stronger defense.

For your Evo and Hero slots, I'd go with Hero Knight, Evo Tesla, and Evo Goblin Barrel. Hero Knight is a great pick in pretty much any meta, and the Evo Tesla can handle a range of enemy pushes. Evo Goblin Barrel is also useful for sneaking in some damage if your opponent fails to spot the real barrel.

How Does Clash Royale’s Power Surge Global Tournament Work?

In the Power Surge tournament, Lightning strikes the arena every so often. It seems to happen roughly every 20 to 30 seconds , though I haven't timed it exactly. The good thing is that Lightning doesn't affect buildings in this mode, so your buildings and towers are safe from it.

You can earn different rewards by winning matches, including chests and Wild Cards. If you want to check your standing, you can tap the 'Wins' section in the middle of the screen to see the Hall of Fame and your tournament ranking.

You can only lose four matches before your tournament run ends, so make sure you choose a deck you can play comfortably.

​

Tips for Clash Royale’s Power Surge Global Tournament

Prefer Cheap Decks

Cheap decks can work really well in Power Surge, so consider swapping expensive cards for cheaper alternatives. For example, Archers cost less than Musketeer or Flying Machine, and all three can die to Lightning. You can cycle back to Archers faster without spending as much elixir. I'd avoid heavy tanks like Giant Skeleton since they will keep getting hit by Lightning and take a lot of damage.

Take Advantage of Buildings

Buildings are immune to Lightning in this mode, so don't be afraid to include them in your deck. I'd even consider running two buildings as they will give you more options on both offense and defense. Siege decks can also take advantage of this, but you will still need to protect your X-Bow or Mortar from enemy troops. The Earthquake is a useful spell to have if your opponent is doing the same thing.

Choose Cards That Can Handle Lightning

Keep Lightning in mind when choosing your cards. The Dark Prince is a good choice because its shield can take a Lightning strike without losing HP. Cheap cards like Bats and Skeletons are also useful since they don't cost much elixir. Even if Lightning takes them out, you won't lose much.

item.title: Yakuza and Attack on Titan Voice Actor Hiroshi Tsuchida Dies at 54
item.description:
Actor Hiroshi Tsuchida, who brought characters to life in game and anime series like Yakuza , Attack on Titan , and myriads of others, has passed away at the age of 54. The loss comes as a shock to those who worked with the actor, including the studio behind Yakuza , as well as his fans.

Hiroshi Tsuchida was born on February 8, 1972. Although gamers and anime fans will recognize his voice from a number of roles in popular series, in Japan, he also frequently provided his voice for the Japanese dubs of multitudes of TV series and films.

Attack On Titan: Every Main Character's Age, Height, And Birthday

Attack On Titan is one of the best-known anime series of the past decade. Here are some basic details fans should know about the main characters.

By Mark Sammut

Hiroshi Tsuchida Passes Away

According to Oricon, Hiroshi Tsuchida's agency announced on October 20 that he passed away on October 11 at the age of just 54. The actor died of heart failure. Tsuchida had a long career in the industry, initially getting his start in live action sentai hero shows back in 1994. While he would continue to appear in and provide his voice to said shows up through 2026, his work extended into anime, video games, and dubbing roles, as well. In the Yakuza franchise, he provided the voice of Kazuki, while he played Grisha Yeager, the father of Erin Yeager, in At tack on Titan . Following the announcement of his loss, his memory has been paid tribute to by fans and by those he worked with, including RGG, the studio behind the Yakuza series.

Tsuchida started voice acting in anime roughly around the same time, with some of his early roles being in a pair of some of the biggest shonen mega-hits, as Raido Namiashi in Naruto , as well as Capote in One Piece . His career appeared to have been going well in recent times, as he continued to perform into 2026, with some of the latest roles being Shippo Marimo in Mebius Dust , and Asakura in Sakamoto Days . His voice could also be heard in the 173rd episode of Black Clover , which premiered on October 17, six days after his passing.

The actor also began acting in video games around the same time that his anime career took off, with his premiere role being Feng Wei in Tekken 5 . He would go on to reprise the role up through Tekken 7 . He was also featured as Zasalamel in Soul Calibur 3 , with him returning for the role in Soulcalibur 4 and 6 . Furthermore, he was also the voice of Tron in the Japanese version of Kingdom Hearts 2 , Maximilian in Dragon's Dogma: Dark Arisen , Kuroda Nagamasa in Nioh , and more.

Hiroshi Tsuchida provided his voice for a number of characters in series that are ongoing or already renewed for new seasons. However, it remains to be seen if he already recorded lines for anime episodes, games, or other media that have yet to be released. Fans have a wide variety of media that they can revisit, should they wish to pay their respects to the actor, but his loss is likely to be keenly felt for a very long time both within the industry and by those who appreciated his talent over the span of his 32-year-long career.
